item.base_system: Mixed multi-element powders of Nb (99.9%), Mo (99.9%), Ta (99.9%), and W (99.9%) with nominal equal atomic percent
item.intervention: Mechanical milling for 2 h followed by drying at 45 °C for 8 h
item.processing: KQM-X/B planetary ball mill, 2 h milling; drying at 45 °C for 8 h
item.structure_change: Powders shaped as spherical or near-spherical; mixed powder absorption rate higher than most powders except Mo
item.attributed_mechanism: Mixing process helps to improve the absorption

item.base_system: NbMoTaW mixed powder on C45 steel substrate
item.intervention: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) with linear energy density of 0.943 J/mm (original process)
item.processing: FORWEDO LM120, 500 W fiber laser, argon atmosphere (<20 ppm O2), ds=0.1 mm, dz=0.1 mm, fp=0.8, v=250 mm/s, S-cross scanning
item.structure_change: Single BCC solid solution formed; smooth surface with metallic luster; experimental lattice parameter 3.2034 Å
item.attributed_mechanism: The SLM process is an effective method to form NbMoTaW HEA
quotes: In this study, a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW alloy was formed by selective laser melting (SLM) with a linear energy density of up to 2.83 J/mm.
The XRD results shown in Figure 3 b, compared with Figure 3 c, illustrate there is only one BCC structure solid solution without another metal phase in the alloy.

item.base_system: NbMoTaW alloy fabricated with original SLM parameters
item.intervention: Additional remelting process: remelting twice for each layer (3 times total laser energy input)
item.processing: Same parameters as original process (v=250 mm/s, ds=0.1 mm, dz=0.1 mm, fp=0.8) but with n=2 remelting times
item.structure_change: Achieved linear energy density up to 2.83 J/mm; composition deviation analyzed
item.attributed_mechanism: Higher energy density is needed for fabricating NbMoTaW HEA parts
quotes: Higher energy density is needed for fabricating NbMoTaW HEA parts, so there was an additional remelting process, which had the same parameters as the original process but underwent remelting twice for each layer, which means that there was 3 times the laser energy input.

item.intervention: Rapid solidification via SLM (high cooling rates)
item.processing: SLM with high density of energy inputs and rapid heat dissipation
item.structure_change: Average grain size 13.4 μm (vs 200 μm in as-cast); primary dendrite arm spacing 6.59 μm (vs 20-30 μm in as-cast); lamellar martensite structure dendrites formed
item.attributed_mechanism: Under the rapid solidification condition of the laser processing, the grains and dendrites as a sub-structure grew and developed with an extremely high temperature gradient and cooling rate
quotes: The average grain size is 13.4 μm, which is much smaller compared with the 200 μm of as-cast NbMoTaW HEA grain size
The primary and secondary dendrite arm spacings are 6.59 μm and 1.68 μm on average, respectively, compared with the as-cast dendrite arm spacing of approximately 20 to 30 μm

item.intervention: Exposure to 3.5%wt NaCl solution for electrochemical testing
item.processing: Three-electrode electrochemical corrosion test; scanning voltage -0.2 V to +0.2 V
item.test_conditions: 3.5%wt NaCl solution, calomel reference electrode, platinum auxiliary electrode
item.property_change: Free-corrosion current I_corrH = 8.716 × 10^-11 A (vs 8.815 × 10^-9 A for 316 L steel); reduced by two orders of magnitude
item.attributed_mechanism: Elements Nb, Mo, and Ta are easy passivation metals, contributing to excellent corrosion resistance
quotes: The free-corrosion current of the HEA is reduced by two orders of magnitude compared with that of the 316 L steel.
The elements Nb, Mo, and Ta contained in the alloy are all the easy passivation metals, which contributes to the excellent corrosion resistance in the 3.5 %wt NaCl solution.

item.intervention: High voltage scanning (-1.5 to +2 V) in 3.5%wt NaCl solution
item.processing: Scanning at high voltage in corrosive environment
item.structure_change: Only crack extension and pitting corrosion observed; no deep corrosion
item.property_change: Corrosion depth negligible compared to 316 L steel (which had depth up to 1 mm)
item.attributed_mechanism: NbMoTaW HEA shows stronger corrosion resistance than 316 L steel
quotes: From Figure 9 a, it is obviously that a strong corrosion happens in 316 L steel, with a corrosion depth of even up to 1 mm.
However, in Figure 9 b, for the NbMoTaW alloy, due to the effect of corrosion, only the crack of the sample has a certain extent of extension.

item.intervention: Analysis of composition deviation due to melting point and density differences
item.processing: EDS analysis and variance calculation of three sintering repeatability experiments
item.structure_change: Segregation of Nb and Mo between inner grains and boundaries; Ta and W distributed evenly
item.property_change: Nb deviation -3.5 at%, Mo deviation -0.16 at% (negative deviation); Ta deviation +3.21 at%
item.attributed_mechanism: Elements with lower melting points arrive at boiling point earlier and evaporate more; lower-density liquid floats to surface and receives more energy
quotes: Mo and Nb, with lower melting points and densities, showed negative deviations of −0.16 at% and −3.5 at%, respectively, compared with the nominal composition of 25%.
In the end, these elements with lower melting points arrive at the boiling point earlier and evaporate more during the SLM process, leading to the negative composition deviation.

item.intervention: Evaluation of plasticity potential based on grain size reduction
